messages:
olivia: Quick heads-up — noticed a p95 spike after the last kernel swap. Prefill time up ~12% on medium-length requests, decode mostly unchanged. anyone else seeing this?

jason: saw the same in canary logs, p99 also drifts on tails during small microbatches (1-4). suspecting kernel-switch path when KV miss rate increases.

mira: added a flamegraph for a 2-token continuation case: prefill dominated by attention kernel select + matmul enqueue. attaching snippet: 
```
# simplified stack samples
prefill_select_kernel 45%
matmul_exec            30%
kv_cache_lookup        10%
other                  15%
```

sasha: interesting — our new fused attention kernel reduces single-op overhead but has higher setup cost. at small batch sizes the setup wins, at larger batch it amortizes. could explain microbatch sizing sensitivity.

olivia: timeline: we rolled kernel v3.7 at 10:23; perf-bot shows p95 jump at 10:27. canary config had batch_timeout=6ms, max_batch=8.

perf-bot: deploy v3.7 -> canary group (10%) at 10:23:12; p95 prefill from 18ms -> 20.2ms (10:27 window); p99 from 40ms -> 44ms.

anita: Hypothesis: for prefill-heavy workloads with short prefixes we should prefer the legacy fast-setup kernel. Proposal: add a transient kernel threshold heuristic: if avg_seq_len < 24 and batch_size < 6 -> prefer fast-setup kernel.

jason: +1 but let's avoid hard thresholds. suggest a tiny cost-model lookup in the scheduler: estimate = alpha*batch_size + beta*avg_seq_len + gamma*(kv_miss_rate) and pick kernel with lower predicted latency. cheap compute.

mira: created a quick experiment matrix: 3 kernel choices x batch_timeouts {4,8,16} x microbatch_sizes {1,2,4,8}. early results: optimal kernel shifts at batch_size>=4; timeout=8ms gives best p95/p99 tradeoff for our mix.

sasha: results look solid. we should also tweak kv prefetch — current policy only warms when prefix_len>32, but many requests have short prefixes with repeated users. propose lowering to 16 with conservative rate-limit to avoid unnecessary memory churn.

olivia: agree. concrete PRs: (1) scheduler cost-model heuristic, (2) dynamic kernel hint based on cost-model, (3) kv prefetch threshold change to 16 with backoff. can we canary these one at a time?

jason: will implement cost-model in the batcher and expose metric "kernel_choice_reason". plan: canary 5% for 24h, compare p50/p95/p99 and tail histograms.

anita: for rollback safety, add automatic fallback: if p95 increases >5% for 30m on canary -> revert kernel hint and disable prefetch.

mira: also adding instrumentation: per-request breakdown fields (prefill_ms, decode_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_setup_ms) to trace. small schema change to traces but helpful.

sasha: small config snippet for the cost model we can use: 
```json
{"alpha": 1.0, "beta": 0.6, "gamma": 8.0, "kernel_penalty": {"fast_setup": 2.0, "fused": 5.5}}
```

jason: sounds good. timeline: I'll have a canary branch by EOD, run 6h smoke then open to 5% traffic.

olivia: thanks — prioritizing this over the other microbatch experiments this sprint. if canary is clean we'll roll to 25% and start the kv-prefetch tweak. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: added metric alerts for kernel-choice-reversion (p95 delta) and kv-prefetch-memory-pressure.

anita: one more ask — let's capture a few long-run traces (>=512 ctx) to ensure no negative interactions with decode path when kernel choice toggles mid-request.

mira: will schedule trace capture on canary hosts and dump to perf bucket.

jason: ok locking plan. follow-up: status update in ~12h with canary numbers.

olivia: perfect, thanks everyone.
